questions.q: How much of Paris had Passepartout been able to see?
choices: Only a rainy view through a carriage window
A whole day of sights with his old friends
The circus in the Champs Elysees one evening
Nothing, because they went around the city
questions.evidence: through the windows of a car, and in a driving rain

questions.q: Why did Passepartout need to go to a shop in Suez?
choices: To buy a newer, more exact watch
To buy shoes and shirts
To send a telegram home to Paris
To buy food for the long voyage to Bombay
questions.evidence: I must buy some shoes and shirts.

questions.q: Why did Passepartout's watch disagree with the time in Suez?
choices: It had been broken when he packed in a hurry
It still showed London time, two hours behind
His great-grandfather had always set it wrong
It ran too fast whenever they were at sea
questions.evidence: You have kept London time, which is two hours behind that of Suez.

questions.q: When Fix said his watch would not agree with the sun, Passepartout replied, "So much the worse for the sun." What does this show about him?
choices: He is stubborn and proud of his family watch
He does not understand how clocks work at all
He is angry with Fix and wants to end the talk
He thinks the sun moves differently in Africa
questions.evidence: returned the watch to its fob with a defiant gesture

questions.q: What did Passepartout tell Fix about how long he had known his master?
choices: He had served Fogg faithfully for ten years
He started work the day they left London
He had known Fogg since they met in Paris
He had worked for Fogg's family as a boy
questions.evidence: I entered his service the very day we left London.

questions.q: Which of these things that Passepartout told Fix made Fix MORE sure that Fogg was the thief?
choices: That Fogg played whist every evening
That Fogg carried a huge sum in new banknotes
That Fogg had a servant who was a Frenchman
That Fogg wanted to see the sights of Egypt
questions.evidence: he is carrying an enormous sum in brand new banknotes with him

questions.q: Once he was fully convinced, Fix "had quite recovered his equanimity." What is equanimity?
choices: Calmness
Speed
Money
Courage
questions.evidence: Fix had quite recovered his equanimity

questions.q: What did Fix do after leaving the consul at the end of the chapter?
choices: He arrested Fogg on the quay at Suez
He sent a telegram and boarded the Mongolia
He went back to the shop to find Passepartout
He waited in Suez for the next steamer
questions.evidence: repaired to the telegraph office, whence he sent the dispatch
